newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare falls, close above support.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare falls, close above support.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared early falls to close slightly down on Friday, buoyed by a recovery in the Dow Jones and late buying ahead of the close of the month.
"The market tended to recover towards the close, due to (portfolio) valuations that need to be made at the close of the month and the quarter," said a floor trader.
"Also, the Dow turned around and that obviously helped," he added.
The blue chip IPC index closed 2.74 points down, or 0.09 percent, at 3,236.79, compared to a session low of 3,203.17. Volume was a dull million shares traded.
Technical analysts pointed out that small trades had an exaggerated effect at low volume, so the IPC could easily have penetrated a support at 3,200 points.
"With the low volume we had it could easily have fallen through, but the rebound was at low volume and there are no indications of a change in downtrend," said a technical analyst.
Fundamental analysts said the market was dulled by apathy among investors, caution ahead of forthcoming earnings reports and concerns over the peso-dollar exchange rate.
"People are worried about ... what may happen with reports," said Carlos Ponce, research director at the Santander brokerage.
"The exchange rate is also making foreign investors shy away from the bourse," he added.

Lagging stocks and selective speculative buying stood out in a session otherwise marked by low volume. The percentage gainers list was led by video rentals stock Video nominal series shares, which are not frequently traded, and followed by financial group Abaco, which traders said gained on speculation that its banking division would raise capital.
Other gaineers were traded at very low volume.
On the broad market, of a total of 107 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered losers 44 to 43, with the remaining 20 unchnaged.
